PRITHVIX

The Connected Agri-Economy

Turning idle machinery, guesswork farming, and invisible labour into a connected, verifiable agri-economy.

Schneider Electric Hackathon | Sustainable Agriculture
TEAM: MADHAV MAHESHWARI
files.note: Welcome to Prithvix. We are building the connected agri-economy to transform rural markets. Right now, idle machinery, guesswork farming, and invisible labour are holding back rural potential. But we can fix that. We turn these hidden inefficiencies into a connected and verifiable system. Let's look at what is holding back sustainable agriculture today.

files.content:
Three Barriers Stifling Sustainable Agriculture
Underutilized Machinery
  • Smallholders cannot afford modern equipment ownership.
  • Informal rental lacks trust infrastructure and transparency.
  • Machinery stays idle 300+ days/year, wasting embodied carbon.
Sustainability Impact
High resource waste and lost regional productivity.
Guesswork Input Application
  • Fertilizer and water applied on a calendar, not on real data.
  • NDVI health data is inaccessible to the average farmer.
  • Blanket application leads to chemical runoff and soil depletion.
Sustainability Impact
Groundwater contamination and ecosystem degradation.
Invisible Rural Labour
  • Labourers have no verifiable reputation or safety records.
  • Informal contractors extract high margins from workers.
  • Lack of accountability leads to unsafe working conditions.
Sustainability Impact
Reduced rural livelihood resilience and social inequity.
TEAM: MADHAV MAHESHWARI
PRITHVIX: THE CONNECTED AGRI-ECONOMY
files.note: Sustainable agriculture faces three major bottlenecks today. First, smallholders cannot afford modern equipment ownership, leaving machinery idle for three hundred days a year while embodied carbon goes to waste. Second, farmers rely on guesswork and calendar-based fertilizer applications instead of real data, causing severe chemical runoff and soil depletion. Third, rural labour remains entirely invisible, lacking basic safety records and falling victim to high margins extracted by informal contractors. These three barriers lead directly to massive resource waste, environmental degradation, and deep social inequity. And trust is the real bottleneck behind every single one of them.

SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE TRACK

A UNIFIED TRUST INFRASTRUCTURE FOR RURAL MARKETS

Trust is the actual bottleneck; Prithvix is the technical unlock.

SCHNEIDER ELECTRIC HACKATHON
TEAM: MADHAV MAHESHWARI
files.note: Trust is the actual bottleneck, and Prithvix is the technical unlock. We provide a unified trust infrastructure built specifically for rural markets. By bringing verification and transparency to every transaction, we bridge the gaps between equipment owners, farmers, and labourers. This creates a secure foundation where sustainable practices actually make economic sense. Now let's examine how this infrastructure drives real systemic sustainability.

files.content:
Driving Systemic Sustainability
Across the Agri-Value Chain
Mapping platform pillars to environmental and social outcomes.
Carbon Reduction
Mechanism: Peer-to-peer machinery sharing marketplace.
Outcome: Lower embodied-carbon footprint per cultivated acre by raising utilization rates and reducing new machine manufacturing.
Waste Reduction
Mechanism: NDVI satellite data + digitized soil health cards.
Outcome: Precision input application reduces fertilizer runoff, prevents groundwater contamination, and protects soil health.
Social Equity
Mechanism: Verified labour marketplace with portable reputation.
Outcome: Fair wage discovery and safety accountability improves rural livelihood resilience and reduces exploitative distress migration.
SCHNEIDER ELECTRIC HACKATHON | SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE
Team: Madhav Maheshwari
files.note: We drive systemic sustainability by aligning our platform pillars directly with environmental and social outcomes. Through our peer-to-peer machinery sharing marketplace, we lower the embodied-carbon footprint per cultivated acre by cutting down the need for new machine manufacturing. By combining satellite NDVI data with digitized soil health cards, we enable precision input application that stops fertilizer runoff and protects groundwater. And through our verified labour marketplace, we establish portable reputations that secure fair wages and improve livelihood resilience. Each mechanism directly targets the core structural flaws of the current agricultural system. Let's trace how a farmer experiences this value chain firsthand.

TEAM: MADHAV MAHESHWARI
CONNECTED AGRI-ECONOMY
files.note: A successful rural platform must guide users seamlessly from the field to the market. The journey starts with an easy onboarding process featuring local language support and voice guidance. Farmers then map their fields by walking boundaries to create digital polygons and unlock satellite NDVI data for stress zone identification. From there, they can rent verified equipment, track operations with real-time GPS geofence alerts, and verify returns using AI-assisted photo condition checks. Every single step removes friction and builds lasting operational trust.

TRUST-TIER SYSTEM
files.note: Operational excellence in sustainable agriculture demands real-time visibility into high-value assets. The marketplace balances dynamic machinery rental scheduling with instant crew dispatch to eliminate idle time and maximize farm yield. By matching supply and demand locally, we turn underutilized tractors and manual labor into fluid, efficient capital. This seamless orchestration lays the groundwork for the robust backend supporting it all. Let us dive into the technical architecture that powers these last-mile operations.

files.content:
A Robust Architecture for Last-Mile Scale
Layer 1: Mobile Clients (Flutter)
One codebase powering two distinct apps (Farmer & Labourer). Shared design system for low-latency iteration and consistent user experience across low-end devices.
Layer 2: API & Edge Functions (Serverless)
Shared jobs/bookings graph connecting demand and supply in real-time. Edge functions handle high-priority geofence breach detection and instant alerting.
Layer 3: Data & Storage
Postgres for relational integrity, live geolocation pipeline for position streaming, and satellite NDVI data ingestion for precision field mapping.
AI/ML Services
  • OCR for soil-card digitization.
  • Face-matching for KYC trust.
  • CV for equipment condition check.
Core Integrations
  • Google Maps / Geolocation.
  • Integrated Payment Gateway.
  • SMS/OTP for secure auth.
TEAM: MADHAV MAHESHWARI
Built for Reliability & Trust
files.note: Scaling across rural markets demands an architecture built for intermittent connectivity and extreme efficiency. We use a lightweight, offline-first backend that synchronizes critical operational data the moment a signal drops back in. Edge caching and modular microservices ensure the platform stays lightning-fast even during peak harvest spikes. This engineering rigor guarantees uninterrupted service where downtime directly threatens crop yields.

files.content:
Reinventing Trust Through Technology
Turning physical presence into cryptographic proof of work.
Geofencing as a Trust Primitive
Not just logistics, but the mechanism that makes peer-to-peer rental psychologically and practically viable for strangers.
AI-Assisted Condition Comparison
Closing the "he-said-she-said" dispute gap that kills trust in informal peer-to-peer machinery markets.
Unified Reputation Layer
Reusing photo+GPS+timestamp verification as core infrastructure across machinery, data, and labour trust.
SCHNEIDER ELECTRIC HACKATHON
Team: Madhav Maheshwari
files.note: Building on our technical architecture, we treat geofencing not just as a boundary tool, but as a core trust primitive. This turns physical presence into cryptographic proof of work, eliminating leakage across rural markets. We close the dispute gap in peer to peer machinery rentals through AI assisted condition comparison. By anchoring digital verification to physical ground truth, we remove the friction of manual auditing. And that unified reputation layer directly drives our projected environmental and social outcomes.

files.content:
Implementation Roadmap: From Blueprint to Field
PRITHVIX EXECUTION PLAN
Phase 0: Prototype
4 Weeks: Working prototype of trust core (Geofencing + KYC).
Phase 1: Pilot
1-3 Months: Deploy in village clusters with real equipment owners.
Phase 2: Satellite
3-6 Months: NDVI layer integrated and KCC wallet live.
Phase 3: Scale
6-12 Months: District-wide scale with strategic partners.
TEAM: MADHAV MAHESHWARI
SCALABLE IMPACT
files.note: Moving from blueprint to field requires a phased rollout that prioritizes regional validation before scaling. We start with a four week prototype of the trust core before deploying into village clusters. Then we integrate satellite NDVI layers and expand systematically across broader rural networks. This disciplined path takes us from initial design straight to full district-wide scale.
